correctness.rationale: For every i<j an ancestor path jumps only by one or two labels; the crossing at i or i-1 gives d(i,j)-h_j in {-h_i,D_i-h_{i-1}}. The neighboring distance D_i is one plus a trailing run of Bernoulli two-step choices; its geometric tail and Borel-Cantelli make the pairwise excess upper bounds tend to minus infinity. A future one-step attachment fuses the two frontier ancestries, giving eventual fixed excess e_i for each i. The maximum K of the e_i is finite and attained, yielding eventual exact diameter H_n+K. An initial 2k-run of two-steps yields K>=k, while union bounds yield P(K>=k)<=2q^k/(1-q) for k>=2. The depth-increment two-state Markov chain has second eigenvalue -q and asymptotic variance pq/(1+q)^3. The standalone checker exactly verified 1,797,528 finite assertions on all 8191 trees of size at most 14 and 75 longer seeded samples; infinite theorems rest on analytical proofs.

originality.rationale: A two-choice Bernoulli recursive-tree diameter-minus-height theorem with pathwise eventual equality, an unbounded finite limiting offset and explicit two-sided exponential bounds was not found in the mathematical-record and accessible own-claim comparisons. The motivating Tang–Wang–Wu source proves one-endedness/collisions and describes branch lengths, which alone is not the same exact metric result. Broutin–Flajolet study a different uniform non-plane binary-tree ensemble; Janson treats broader tree limits. Full text of the motivating source was inaccessible, so possible implicit coverage is a material residual risk and priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Diameter and root height are fundamental, naturally defined global metric statistics. The theorem shows an eventually exact sample-path relation with a genuinely random, unbounded yet exponentially tailed offset, rather than just a shared linear scale; its root-height Markov reduction also yields the explicit asymptotic variance for the diameter. The all-n eventual identity and tail bounds need the ancestor-cut argument, are not a numerical exercise, and give future leverage for metric and random-walk estimates on the newly studied tree ensemble.
